entries.name: AvgKdegs.csv
entries.source: RNADecayCafe v1.1, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.16884513
entries.why: target for nexus_txn: k_syn = avg_RPKM_total * avg_kdeg, 8,867 usable K562 genes

entries.name: k562_atac.bed.gz
entries.source: ENCODE ENCFF926KTI, K562 ATAC-seq IDR thresholded peaks, GRCh38, 55,575 peaks
entries.why: nexus_txn L2 promoter accessibility. NOT the original file, which is lost

entries.name: re2g_k562.bed.gz
entries.source: ENCODE-rE2G ENCSR627ANP / ENCFF976OKL, K562 thresholded element-gene links, 87,490
entries.why: raw source for _abcfeat.json

entries.name: lambert.csv
entries.source: Lambert et al. 2018, Human TFs database v1.01
entries.why: raw source for lambert_tf_symbols.json

entries.name: ctcf_gw.bed.gz
entries.source: ENCODE ENCFF362OPG, K562 CTCF IDR thresholded, ENCSR000AKO, GRCh38, 44,104 peaks
entries.why: the 0.663 CRISPR bar. NOT the original file; rebuilt bar reads 0.6737 against 0.6632

entries.name: GSM8523629_supercoil_rep1_hg38.bw
entries.source: GEO GSE277502, bTMP-seq hTERT-RPE1, hg38, 20 kb bins
entries.why: torsion attempt 1

entries.name: GSM8523630_supercoil_rep2_hg38.bw
entries.source: GEO GSE277502 replicate 2
entries.why: replicate-concordance control, r = 0.796

entries.name: GSM8523628_RPE1_bTMP_genomic_control_hg38.bw
entries.source: GEO GSE277502 naked genomic DNA control
entries.why: the matched control GSE285699 does not ship

entries.name: GSM8706920_1_RPKM.bw
entries.source: GEO GSE285699, TMP-seq SH-SY5Y WT rep1, hg38, 70-90 bp run-length encoded
entries.why: torsion attempt 2; carries the twin-domain z = +23.21

entries.name: GSM8706924_5_RPKM.bw
entries.source: GEO GSE285699 WT rep2
entries.why: replicate for attempt 2

entries.name: _abcfeat.json
entries.source: aggregated from ENCODE-rE2G by build_abcfeat() in this file
entries.why: nexus_txn L3. The ORIGINAL came from ABC and has no producer anywhere in this repo

entries.name: lambert_tf_symbols.json
entries.source: filtered from Lambert v1.01 by build_lambert() in this file
entries.why: nexus_txn L4, 1,639 TFs

entries.name: HumanGEM.xml
entries.source: Human-GEM (SysBioChalmers), SBML, 12,931 reactions / 8,461 metabolites / 2,848 genes
entries.why: the stoichiometry cell_loop closes the growth feedback through; cell_complete's own metabolism is 3,355 reaction STRINGS with no stoichiometric matrix behind them

entries.name: clinvar.vcf.gz
entries.source: NCBI ClinVar, GRCh38 VCF, 4,461,717 records
entries.why: the variant-addressable slot loop_variant built: 4,443 genes with pathogenic missense and 14,987 with benign missense. NOTE this file is REGENERATED WEEKLY by NCBI, so the hash will drift and a mismatch here means a newer release, not corruption

entries.name: ctcf_gm12878_hg19.bed.gz
entries.source: ENCODE ENCSR000AKB / ENCFF833FTF, GM12878 CTCF optimal IDR peaks, hg19, 40,790 peaks
entries.why: the barrier landscape the whole extrusion model runs on. CELL-TYPE MATCHED to the Hi-C rather than borrowed from K562, and hg19 to match the map -- the project's other CTCF file is K562/GRCh38 and would have been a silent double mismatch

entries.name: hg19_chr21.fa.gz
entries.source: UCSC hg19 chr21
entries.why: CTCF motif ORIENTATION, scanned with JASPAR MA0139.1. Orientation is the entire mechanism -- a forward site blocks a leftward leg and a reverse site a rightward one -- and it is not in the peak file, so it has to come from sequence. Also supplies GC and CpG

entries.name: hg19_chr22.fa.gz
entries.source: UCSC hg19 chr22
entries.why: the HELD-OUT chromosome. loop_surrogate's whole result -- physics 0.2852 against a trained CNN's 0.0893 -- depends on chr22 never having been fitted

entries.name: ctcf_pfm.json
entries.source: JASPAR MA0139.1, CTCF, 19 bp position frequency matrix
entries.why: the motif whose direction decides which way a barrier faces

entries.name: HumanGEM_genes.tsv
entries.source: Human-GEM gene table, 2,848 Ensembl IDs with gene symbols
entries.why: REQUIRED, and its absence is silent. The SBML ships EMPTY gene names, so any module that reads cobra's g.name gets an Ensembl ID and every symbol join returns nothing. That cost loop_buffering two full runs reporting its isozyme features at exactly 0.5000 -- the signature of a column that was never computed, not of a feature that does not work

entries.name: GSE63525_GM12878_insitu_primary_30.hic
entries.source: Rao 2014 GM12878 in situ primary, the deepest published human Hi-C, hg19
entries.why: the target the whole 4D arc is scored against. NEVER DOWNLOADED -- hicstraw range-requests one chromosome, so a ~20 GB file costs ~20 s and ~700k records. There is no local hash because there is no local copy, and that is recorded rather than hidden. The replicate file (…_insitu_replicate_30.hic) is read the same way and gives the 0.9285 ceiling

entries.name: ens_gtf.gz
entries.source: Ensembl 112 GRCh38 annotation; only the CDS lines are read
entries.why: the exon structure that makes loop_chain's genomic-coordinate-to-codon walk possible. Without it a point mutation cannot be carried to an amino acid at all, and the middle link of the chain would have to be a lookup instead of a computation

entries.name: ens_cds.fa.gz
entries.source: Ensembl 112 coding sequences, one per transcript
entries.why: the codon itself. Paired with the GTF this gives the reference base at every variant, which is what let loop_chain check its own translation: 100.00% reference-base agreement over 966,223 variants, before ClinVar's consequence field was ever consulted

entries.name: skempi_v2.csv
entries.source: SKEMPI 2.0, measured binding free-energy changes for mutations in protein complexes
entries.why: the only MEASURED interface data here, and the task nexus was actually validated on. loop_nexus_fair needs it as a positive control: without it there is no way to tell a sensor that does not work from a harness that does not work

entries.name: sider_se.tsv.gz
entries.source: SIDER 4.1, drug side effects from package inserts, STITCH compound ids x MedDRA terms
entries.why: the ONLY compound-to-adverse-event data anywhere in this project; `side effect` had 48 gene-disease rows and nothing else

entries.name: sider_names.tsv
entries.source: SIDER 4.1 compound id to drug name
entries.why: the join from SIDER's STITCH ids to cell_complete's drug NAMES

entries.name: intogen.zip
entries.source: IntOGen 2024-06-18 driver compendium, Compendium_Cancer_Genes.tsv
entries.why: cancer driver labels; the `cancer` row had 839 items and no held-out target

entries.name: HumanGEM_genes.tsv
entries.source: Human-GEM gene annotation table, ENSG -> symbol / Entrez / UniProt
entries.why: the join between Human-GEM's ENSG ids and everything else here, which is keyed on symbol

entries.name: gnomad_loeuf.txt.bgz
entries.source: gnomAD v2.1.1 per-gene loss-of-function constraint
entries.why: the source of cell_complete's loeuf column, and the one field that reproduces EXACTLY -- 1.0000 exact over 15,038 genes. That exactness is what pins the version: v2.1.1 and not v4, which would have shown the same drift the coordinates do

entries.name: cpgIslandExt.txt.gz
entries.source: UCSC hg38 CpG islands, Gardiner-Garden and Frommer calls
entries.why: the source of the cpg column. It is the right track -- agreement rises from 0.72 to 0.92 when the query point moves to the file's own tss -- but no declared rule reaches the 0.90 gate, so the field is recorded as unverified rather than claimed

entries.name: goa_human.gaf.gz
entries.source: GO annotations for human, current release
entries.why: fetched for cell_complete's proc and comp columns and NOT used for them. Those are each one of exactly 12 buckets and the GO-term-to-bucket map is recorded nowhere, so the ontology is retrievable and the coarsening is not. Kept because that gap is the finding

log: THE DATA LEDGER -- every external input, where it came from, and how to get it back
Four inputs nexus_txn needs were absent from this container, so a recorded result could be
read but not checked. Recovering them took a Zenodo search, three ENCODE queries, a GEO
crawl and a rebuild from a different predictor. That knowledge lived only in commit
messages. This file makes it executable.
REBUILD CHECK -- a derived file must reproduce its hash from its raw inputs, or the
recorded transform is not the one that made it
Every derived file rebuilds bit-identically. The transforms in this file ARE the ones
that produced them, so the provenance claim is checkable rather than asserted.
TO RESTORE ANYTHING MISSING:  python3 colab/data_ledger.py --fetch <name|all>
STILL NOT IN THIS LEDGER, and still the biggest hole, but smaller than it was:
cell_complete.json is 38 MB, read by 227 modules, gitignored, and has no external source
to fetch from. It is a DERIVED artefact whose original producer is lost. It now has a
PARTIAL one -- colab/build_cell_complete.py rebuilds 8 of its 27 per-gene fields from the
three sources added above plus the Ensembl GTF and Lambert, and CHECKS each against the
surviving copy: 7 agree, cpg does not, and 17% of all module-reads are now backed by a
named source rather than by the file's continued existence. The other 83% is classified,
which is not the same as recovered: 30% has a URL and no download, 20% has real data with
the rule or the source unrecorded, 6% is labels this project invented and cannot rebuild.
A ledger cannot close that; only the missing downloads and the lost rules can.
